profiles.summary: No new opcode or call difference was found. I read the transfer precompile source again for its balance check.

deltas.delta: The transfer precompile moves value with the journal transfer function and returns a halt when that function reports an error, so it cannot move more than the source account holds. From Jovian on it no longer resets the cold status of the two accounts.

profiles.summary: The fee currency debit and credit are steps of the transaction handler. The debit runs before the main call and its transient storage is cleared. The credit runs after the main call has returned and clears transient storage when it ends. No contract can start either step from inside a call.

deltas.delta: debit_gas_fees uses the system call path that does not commit (erc20.rs line 95). The handler wraps it in a journal checkpoint and, after the checkpoint is committed, calls transient_storage.clear() (handler.rs lines 695 to 698). The main call therefore starts with an empty transient map.

credit_gas_fees uses the committing system call path (erc20.rs line 134). call_inner clears transient storage after that call (core_contracts.rs lines 241 to 248). The credit sees the transient values the main call left and nothing after it can read them.

For a transaction that pays gas in a fee currency the handler rejects the transaction when its value exceeds the sender's native balance (handler.rs lines 805 to 815). A deposit's mint is added to the sender balance before that check (line 773). The value itself moves in the call frame as on Ethereum.

profiles.summary: By value the PoolManager's largest holdings are wBRL, wARS and G$, followed by small amounts of USDC, USDT and CELO. G$ is frozen for the PoolManager address by the token owner since 11 September 2026. Every other pooled token that was probed moves one to one in both directions.

Read from chain at block 83,475,210: 3,193,624.74 wBRL (83.7 percent of the 3,816,971.75 supply), 226,945,961.04 wARS (59.0 percent of supply), 550,022,104.46 G$ (13.7 percent of supply), 4,958.43 USDC, 4,648.08 USDT, 6,167.15 CELO, 11,689,244.47 COPm, 6,312.58 KESm and 54.12 USDm.

It is an OpenZeppelin upgradeable ERC-20 with a pauser role, a minter role, a compliance role that can switch on a blocklist checked for sender and recipient, and an upgrader role for UUPS upgrades. enforceBlocklist(), isBlocked(PoolManager) and paused() all return false on both tokens.

G$ (0x62B8B11039FcfE5aB0C56E502b1C372A3d2a9c7A) is a proxy of the verified contract SuperGoodDollar at 0xb4419A3Df33b9aa6fbE452Df8816389E599C29eF. G$ charges a transfer fee through a formula contract (0x1151867dA39003695eEd28fAfa871079C91884C9). getFees returns a fee of zero for amounts of 10^18 and 10^24 and for transfers that name the PoolManager as sender or recipient. profiles.summary: G$ depends on the Superfluid host, a protocol contract that computes balances from agreements. A flaw in that host let an attacker stream 2.8 billion unbacked G$ in September 2026, and the token owner answered with the block on the PoolManager. Calls from the PoolManager address to the wrapped native predeploy and the EntryPoints were measured and book value one to one.

deltas.delta: G$ reports getHost() 0xA4Ff07cF81C02CFD356184879D953970cA957585. balanceOf is the real time balance that the host's agreements produce, floored at zero. The token source states that a blocked account can still be credited through agreements, and that for a blocked account it rejects agreement writes that open or raise an outflow or lower the account balance.

Superfluid's report on the incident of 3 September 2026 says an operator registered Super Apps on Celo without permission checks, that a terminate callback returning about 900 KB of data made stream closure and liquidation exceed the 30,000,000 block gas limit, that 2,801,252,167 unbacked G$ resulted, and that the host was upgraded on 4 September with a cap on callback return data and with Super App whitelisting switched back on.

GoodDollar's post-mortem of 20 October 2026 says transfers from G$ liquidity pools were blocked, that all pools were unblocked on 28 September except the Celo Uniswap v4 pool, which holds 550 million G$, and that the pool stays blocked until the position holder contacts Good Labs or moves the position to the Good Labs Safe 0x4e31993d9F13F940828bf9eC2f643A7E55B21e8C.

Measured with the PoolManager as caller: a value call of 10^15 wei with empty calldata raises balanceOf(PoolManager) on the wrapped native predeploy 0x4200000000000000000000000000000000000006 and on the three EntryPoints by exactly 10^15. A zero value call raises nothing. transfer on the predeploy moves 10^15 of the wrapped token and releases no native value. transfer on each EntryPoint reverts. L2ToL1MessagePasser and the SequencerFeeVault keep the value and have no balanceOf.
deltas.source: eth_call on https://forno.celo.org with a state override that places the runtime code of Multicall3 (0xcA11bde05977b3631167028862bE2a173976CA11) at the PoolManager address and at a second address, 2026-11-22

profiles.summary: Nothing new at the opcode level in this cycle.

I read the fee and balance step of the X Layer handler again for value handling. A gasless transaction needs a sender balance that covers its value, and a deposit adds its mint before execution. No path gives a call frame value that the sender does not hold.

deltas.delta: In validate_against_state_and_deduct_caller a gasless transaction is rejected when the sender balance is below the transaction value, and the balance is then written back unchanged (handler.rs lines 178 to 188). For a deposit the mint is added to the sender balance and the value is left to the call frame (lines 113 to 143). The branch that raises the balance to the value runs only when the node has the balance check disabled, which is a simulation setting.

findings.title: The GoodDollar owner has blocked the PoolManager address on Celo, so 550 million G$ held for pools cannot leave
findings.difference: G$ on Celo is a Superfluid Super Token with an owner controlled list of accounts that can neither send nor receive it, and with an owner function that burns from any account. After the Superfluid incident of September 2026 the owner put the Uniswap v4 PoolManager on that list and has not removed it. Ethereum's PoolManager holds no token in this state.
findings.mechanism: 1. On 11 September 2026 at 13:48:08 UTC (Celo block 77,233,730, transaction 0x22cd34a5f179dfa342fd3659d029e4d40469ca8fa02abd032145f162b0b8dd4d, sent by 0x6823a04a6fd4148167567d5ef6dcca1f34db0494 to the contract 0xa2521e8f5a990903fdd8afa6570c52526e7e0d5e) the token emitted BlockedUpdated with value true for eleven addresses, one of which is the PoolManager 0x288dc841A52FCA2707c6947B3A777c5E56cd87BC. setBlocked is restricted to the owner role. isBlocked(PoolManager) returned true at block 83,475,285 on 22 November 2026. 2. Every ERC-20, ERC-677 and ERC-777 movement of G$ runs _processFees, which reverts with SUPER_GOODDOLLAR_BLOCKED (0xe7d0c09e) when the sender or the recipient is blocked. An eth_call of transfer from the PoolManager reverts with that selector for amounts 1 and 0. A transfer of 1 unit from the owner account to the PoolManager reverts the same way, and the same transfer to another address returns true. 3. take debits the caller and then calls transfer on the currency (src/PoolManager.sol:291-297). A failed transfer makes take revert (src/types/Currency.sol:64-86). Every take of G$ therefore reverts, including a take of zero. The PoolManager's 550,022,104.456 G$ stay where they are. 4. A position owner who removes liquidity from a G$ pool receives a positive G$ delta. The owner can take the other currency. For the G$ side the remaining choices are mint, which turns the delta into an ERC-6909 claim (src/PoolManager.sol:322-329), and clear, which gives it up (src/PoolManager.sol:310-319). A swap that buys G$ ends the same way. 5. A payment of G$ into the PoolManager by transfer reverts as well, so a seller needs a G$ claim to burn (src/PoolManager.sol:332-336). The token source says a blocked account can still be credited through Superfluid agreements. Such a credit would raise balanceOf(PoolManager), and sync followed by settle would credit it to the settler (src/PoolManager.sol:279-288, 349-364). I did not simulate that path. 6. The owner can also call adminBurn(account, amount), which skips allowance, hooks, pause and the block list. A burn of the PoolManager's balance would leave pool liquidity and G$ claims without tokens behind them. Superfluid's report says 544 million G$ was burned elsewhere during the recovery.
findings.impact: 550,022,104 G$, which is 13.7 percent of the G$ supply and about 60,000 USD at the price Blockscout shows (0.00010924 USD). GoodDollar names one position holder with two wallets as the depositor. Because all pools share one address, the block also covers every other G$ pool in this PoolManager, every G$ claim and any protocol fee accrued in G$. The paired currencies of those pools can still be withdrawn.
findings.preconditions: None remain. The block is in force. It ends when an account with the G$ owner role calls setBlocked with false for the PoolManager. owner() returns 0x495d133b938596c9984d462f007b676bdc57ecec. GoodDollar states it will do so once the position holder contacts Good Labs or moves the position to the Good Labs Safe.
findings.mitigations: The deployer cannot lift the block. Interfaces should stop routing through G$ pools on Celo and should show G$ positions as withdrawable only as claims. Liquidity providers can remove liquidity, take the paired currency and mint the G$ side as a claim. Integrations should not value G$ claims or G$ pool liquidity at the market price while the block and the admin burn function exist. New deployments should treat any token with a per address block list as able to freeze every pool of that token at once.

findings.title: Issuers of the tokens that make up most pool value on Celo and X Layer can pause, block, burn or upgrade the PoolManager's balance
findings.difference: The pooled value on these two networks sits in issuer controlled tokens that are small or new: wBRL and wARS on Celo, and USDT0, USDG, two USDC contracts and tokenized stocks on X Layer. On Celo the PoolManager holds 83.7 percent of all wBRL and 59.0 percent of all wARS. Each of these tokens has roles that act on a single holder address.
findings.mechanism: 1. All pools keep a currency in one balance at the PoolManager address, and that balance leaves only through transfer inside take (src/PoolManager.sol:291-297, src/types/Currency.sol:64-86). A role that stops transfers for that one address stops every pool of the token. 2. wBRL and wARS are proxies of LatamStable. Its compliance role can switch the blocklist on and block the PoolManager, after which _update reverts for it as sender and as recipient. Its pauser role stops all transfers. Its upgrader role can replace the implementation through UUPS and with it the balance logic. The blocklist is switched off today and neither token is paused. 3. On X Layer USDT0 has addToBlockedList and destroyBlockedFunds, USDG has freeze and wipeFrozenAddress, both USDC contracts have a blacklister and a pause, and xETH has a deny list and a pause. A wipe or a destroy sets the PoolManager balance to zero while pool accounting and ERC-6909 claims still count the tokens. 4. BMNRx and ANTx report balanceOf as shares times a multiplier that a multiplier updater role sets, and a fee per period can lower the multiplier over time. A lower multiplier lowers balanceOf(PoolManager) without a take, which leaves pools with less than their accounting says (assumption A2). A higher multiplier adds tokens that no settle credits. The multiplier is 1.0 and the fee is 0 today. 5. On Celo the owner of USDm, which is Celo Governance, can name operators and burners that move or burn the balance of any account. 6. core has no function that reacts to any of these actions. Liquidity providers who exit first after a partial loss take the remaining tokens, and later exits revert when the balance runs out.
findings.impact: On Celo about 522,000 USD of wBRL and 129,000 USD of wARS at the prices Blockscout shows, plus the USDC paired with them. On X Layer about 5.97 million USDT0, 459,000 USDG and 97,700 USDC, plus the 4.67 million USDe that trade against USDT0 in the largest pool. USDe itself has no block or pause function in its code. A freeze stops withdrawals of the affected token for every pool. A wipe, burn or lower multiplier is a loss shared by all liquidity providers and claim holders of that token.
findings.preconditions: An action by a role holder of the token: compliance, pauser or upgrader for wBRL and wARS, the owner of USDT0 (0x4dff9b5b0143e642a3f63a5bcf2d1c328e600bf8), the asset protection role of USDG, the blacklister or pauser of each USDC contract, the multiplier updater or owner of the stock tokens, and the owner of USDm, which is Celo Governance (0xD533Ca259b330c7A88f74E000a3FaEa2d63B7972). No such flag is set for the PoolManager on either chain at blocks 83,476,610 (Celo) and 76,608,329 (X Layer).
findings.mitigations: Liquidity providers should size positions in these tokens with the issuer roles in mind, and pool interfaces should show them. Monitoring should watch the PoolManager address in each token's block, freeze and pause state and the stock token multiplier. Pools in rebasing stock tokens should use the wrapped ERC-4626 versions, which keep a fixed balance. The deployer cannot remove any of these roles.

findings.title: X Layer block builder can exclude PoolManager transactions through a rule driven risk control filter, which leaves L1 deposits as the exit
findings.difference: Ethereum has no protocol component that screens transactions by content. The X Layer execution client contains a risk control filter in the block builder. It evaluates every pool transaction after simulation against rules supplied by an external service, using the transaction's logs, call frames and native transfers. A second component drops transactions that emit bridge events for a configured token.
findings.mechanism: 1. All funds of all pools sit at one address and leave only through take (src/PoolManager.sol:291-297), which runs inside unlock (src/PoolManager.sol:104-114). An exit is a transaction that the sequencer must include. 2. A rule that matches PoolManager events, calls into the PoolManager or transfers of a pooled token gives a deny verdict. The builder then marks the transaction invalid and removes it from the pool, so it is never included. An audit verdict holds the transaction until the external service approves it. 3. New in this cycle, read on the main branch: the builder also denies a transaction when its capture exceeds an observation limit (10,000 native transfers, 10,000 event bindings or 10,000 call frame observations), when the observed frame stack is unbalanced, and when no rule snapshot was pinned for the block although screening is enabled. With the filter enabled, every pool transaction screened in a block without a pinned rule snapshot is denied and removed from the pool. 4. Deposits are outside the filter. The builder source states that a deposit is consensus mandated and that the rule result for it is reported and never acted on. A user can call the same contracts through OptimismPortal.depositTransaction on Ethereum from the same EOA. Contract accounts arrive with an aliased sender, so a position held by an L2 contract needs an EOA that the contract accepts as caller. Finding F-046 records a separate rule that can void a deposit whose source hash is on the deposit blacklist. 5. FilterConfig::default() sets enabled to false, the filter needs a service URL to start, and the setting is read once at node start. The crate header names a requirement 'OKONE Mainnet RSC'. Whether the mainnet sequencer starts with the filter enabled cannot be read from chain. The public endpoint reports the build reth/v2.3.0-f60420a with xlayer/v0.0.7 and refuses rpc_modules, and I found no operator statement about the mainnet setting.
findings.impact: While a matching rule is active, liquidity providers and swappers cannot move funds through sequencer submitted transactions in the affected pools, or in all pools if the rule targets the PoolManager address. No funds are lost. Exit through an L1 deposit costs Ethereum gas and depends on the sequencer following derivation.
findings.preconditions: The sequencer operator must run with the filter enabled and the risk control service must deliver a rule that matches PoolManager activity, or leave a block without a pinned rule snapshot. Whether the mainnet sequencer has the filter or the bridge interceptor enabled, and which rules are loaded, is still unconfirmed after this cycle. The filter entered the code in release v0.0.7, and operators had to upgrade to v0.0.7.3 by 10 November 2026.
findings.mitigations: Liquidity providers who hold positions through contracts should keep an EOA controlled path so that an L1 deposit can reach the position. Integrators can prepare the L1 deposit route to the PositionManager in advance. The deployer can ask OKX to state whether the filter runs on mainnet and which contracts and tokens its rules may match.

cleared.check: Leads L-153 and L-202 for Celo: does the fee currency debit or credit, or any other client feature, run code inside a call in progress under a transient storage map separate from the caller's while keeping its transfers and storage writes.
cleared.result: No. The debit and the credit are steps of the transaction handler and run before the first frame of the main call and after its last frame has returned. A contract cannot start them. The debit starts from the empty map of a new transaction and the handler clears its transient writes before the main call (handler.rs lines 695 to 698). The credit runs on the same journal as the main call and clears transient storage when it ends (core_contracts.rs lines 241 to 248). The fee currency must be registered in FeeCurrencyDirectory, which Governance owns, so the code that runs is not chosen by the caller. The other system calls of the client read exchange rates through call_read_only, which reverts everything it did. unlock is one call frame (src/PoolManager.sol:104-114), so neither step can separate a take from its debit.

cleared.check: Lead L-203 on both chains: can a call frame carry value that the caller's balance did not lose in the same journal (fee currency transactions and deposits with mint on Celo, gasless transactions and deposits on X Layer, the transfer precompile).
cleared.result: No. On Celo a fee currency transaction is rejected when its value exceeds the sender's native balance, a deposit's mint is added to the sender before execution, and the value then moves in the call frame (handler.rs lines 773 and 805 to 815). The transfer precompile uses the journal transfer and halts on an error, and it accepts only the CELO token as caller (transfer.rs lines 52 to 57 and 91 to 125). On X Layer a gasless transaction is rejected when the sender balance is below the value and the balance is otherwise left as it is, and a deposit adds its mint first (handler.rs lines 113 to 143 and 178 to 188). The one branch that raises a balance to the value runs only with the balance check disabled, which block production does not use. A native credit in core is msg.value (src/PoolManager.sol:352-354), and on both chains that value has left the caller's balance.

The underlying token sits in the wrapper contract and the PoolManager holds none of it, so the two ids do not share a balance. leadResults.answer: For Celo only. The fee currency debit and credit are handler steps around the main call and no contract can start them from inside a call. The debit starts with an empty transient map and its transient writes are cleared before the main call (celo-kona handler.rs lines 695 to 698). The credit runs after the main frame has returned, on the same journal, and clears transient storage at its end (core_contracts.rs lines 241 to 248). Neither shape named in the lead exists. Details are in the cleared list.

For Celo only. The only features that run code outside the main call are the fee currency debit and credit and the read only rate lookups. They run code of contracts that Governance registered, they cannot be started by a contract, the debit's transient map is discarded before the main call, and the credit shares the main map after unlock has returned and locked (src/PoolManager.sol:112-113). No inner run can pay tokens in and settle, and no take can lose its debit.

For Celo and X Layer only. Source lines read in this cycle: Celo rejects a fee currency transaction whose value exceeds the native balance and adds a deposit mint before execution (handler.rs lines 773, 805 to 815). X Layer rejects a gasless transaction whose sender balance is below the value and adds a deposit mint before execution (op-revm handler.rs lines 113 to 143, 178 to 188). Value moves in the call frame in every case. The Celo transfer precompile accepts only the CELO token as caller and fails when the source balance is too low.

For Celo and X Layer only. Measured with the PoolManager as caller through a state override: the wrapped native predeploys, Wrapped OKB and the three EntryPoints raise balanceOf(PoolManager) by exactly the value sent, and nothing on a zero value call. The wrappers transfer one to one and release no native value, and the EntryPoints have no transfer. No address with a different rate or unit was found among the value accepting addresses of the earlier sweep.
